story_type: F-35C carrier arrested landings day and night, aviator stress story, new GPS landing system test
hook: Pilots said this was more stressful than combat.
narration: This was more stressful than combat.
In Vietnam, the story goes, aviators were wired with stress sensors.
The worst readings came from landing on a carrier at night.
This is the F-35C, tested aboard USS Abraham Lincoln in 2018.
Its tailhook must snag a steel wire that stops it in two seconds.
The Lincoln was testing a new landing system called JPALS.
Five sensors on the ship turn GPS data into the ship's position and send it to the jet.
At the time, the Lincoln was the only carrier with it installed.
outcome: The F-35C caught the wire and stopped on the Lincoln's deck.
title: Carrier landings beat combat for stress
description:
F-35C Lightning II jets landed aboard USS Abraham Lincoln in August 2018 while the ship tested JPALS, a GPS-based landing system, for the Navy's Operational Test and Evaluation Force.
